text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand. When developers refactor, they clean up messy sections, remove duplicate lines, and give variables clearer names. This makes the code simpler for everyone on the team. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up over time when quick fixes are used instead of proper solutions. By regularly refactoring, teams keep their projects healthy and avoid bigger problems later. Remember, if the behavior changes, it is not refactoring — it is something else.
